If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33 over 3 days) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to dampen momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to offset downward bias.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below 65% of recent high, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for late horizon to capture rebound potential.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is above 65% of recent low, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for late horizon to avoid overcorrection.
